page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v7 is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 variants, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), delivering hardware acceleration for matrix math and vector calculations.

System memory totals 512.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per vCPU. Hardware benchmarks reveal strong multi-core performance, achieving 63,502.15 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 80,219.92. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 329.32 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 147.79 GB/sec for writes. Single-core stress-ng tests register in the middle tier at 2,206.19, while single-core Geekbench scores rank in the upper quartile at 2,127.0.

The E64s_v7 contains no bundled local storage and zero included public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote attached premium managed disks for root filesystem and persistent application data. Acceleration hardware is omitted, featuring zero discrete GPUs. From a resource-density perspective, the machine provides substantial memory capacity paired with dedicated compute, though the absence of ephemeral NVMe requires balancing external block storage latency against memory access speeds.

This hardware profile is targeted toward large in-memory databases, key-value stores, distributed analytics, and enterprise data processing. Benchmark results validate this focus, demonstrating 105.13 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 29,091.56 in PassMark database transaction tests.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz across 32 physical cores, the instance features a 480 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions. The instance has no integrated local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on networked block storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the E64s_v7 registers upper-quartile multi-core processing with a PassMark CPU score of 80,219.92 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 329.32 GB/sec. It delivers high throughput on memory-centric tasks, achieving 105.13 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The hardware profile is engineered primarily for memory-intensive workloads, including enterprise relational databases, large-scale in-memory caches, distributed analytics engines, and batch transaction processing pipelines.
